name: Email Authentication
description: Collect published SPF, DKIM and DMARC TXT records for a hostname or domain into email-authentication MISP objects.
requirements: DNS access to a recursive resolver
output: misp_standard: the original attribute and one email-authentication object per matching TXT resource record, linked to the original attribute by derived-from.
features: Query SPF at the exact input name and DMARC at _dmarc.<input>. Query DKIM at <selector>._domainkey.<input> for each configured selector.
Normalize names to lowercase IDNA, use absolute DNS queries, and disable resolver search paths. DNS CNAME resolution is handled by dnspython.
Concatenate character-string chunks within each TXT resource record without inserting spaces. Separate TXT resource records remain separate objects, including multiple published SPF or DMARC records.
Keep the original queried domain, query name, returned TXT owner, TTL and raw concatenated policy/key text. Record first_seen and last_seen as the UTC observation time of this lookup.
Use a request-local resolver, four workers, a per-query timeout and a shared elapsed-time budget. Keep successful records when another query fails and describe failures in the first object's comment.

Treat NXDOMAIN and NoAnswer as no records returned. Report timeouts, resolver failures, invalid UTF-8 TXT records, truncation and exhausted time budgets separately. If nothing matches, return an explanatory error, including any failures.
All new attributes have to_ids=false. Preserve the original attribute UUID and metadata. The module never populates message evaluation fields such as spf, dkim, dmarc or dkim-signature.

nameserver.description: Optional IPv4 or IPv6 address of a recursive DNS resolver. A fresh resolver is created for every request.

dkim_selectors.description: Comma-separated selectors replacing the default list, with duplicates removed. At most 32 selectors, including dotted selectors, are supported. Empty or unset uses the default list.

query_timeout.description: Seconds per DNS lookup, between 0.1 and 10. Each lookup is also limited to the remaining shared time budget.

max_time.description: Shared DNS time budget in seconds, between 1 and 25. Queued queries are skipped after the deadline. DNS retry scheduling and object serialization can add a small amount of overhead.

object_template.name: email-authentication
object_template.description: Proposed version-2 extension of the merged version-1 template. Retains every original relation and its meaning. Adds domain, dns-name, dns-owner, dns-ttl, dkim-selector, spf-record, dkim-record and dmarc-record. Adds the three record relations to requiredOneOf so both message observations and published DNS record observations validate. This extension is bundled locally; it has not been submitted to misp-objects.
object_template.installation: The module loads its bundled definition, so an older PyMISP object catalog works. Before importing results into MISP, install this definition as objects/email-authentication/definition.json in the MISP server's misp-objects checkout (usually app/files/misp-objects), then update object templates through MISP administration. Keep the same UUID and version 2. Coordinate this local change with future misp-objects updates.

limitations: Published policies and keys do not prove SPF, DKIM or DMARC success or failure for a message. No message, sending IP, envelope sender, signature, or alignment evaluation is performed.

DNS cannot enumerate all DKIM selectors. Supply selectors from message headers or provider documentation when known. Missing records for the tested selectors do not establish that DKIM is disabled. Empty p= keys are retained as published revoked keys.

Lookups use exactly the input domain or hostname. They do not replace a hostname with its registered domain or perform organizational-domain DMARC fallback. A missing _dmarc record at a subdomain does not establish that no inherited DMARC policy applies.

SPF include/redirect mechanisms are retained without recursive evaluation. TXT detection identifies candidate records; it does not validate policy syntax, cryptographic keys, DNSSEC or policy effectiveness. Multiple policy records are preserved without selecting one.
Only SPF, DKIM and DMARC TXT records are collected. MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, BIMI, SMTP probes and HTTP policy fetching are outside this module's scope.
Return at most 20 matching TXT records per query. Non-UTF-8 TXT records are skipped with a warning. Resolver caching may affect observed TTLs.
installation: Install misp-modules with its minimal or all dependency extra; dnspython is already declared there. No new dependency or API key is needed.
Install the bundled version-2 template on the MISP server as described above, restart misp-modules, and enable email_authentication in MISP Enrichment settings.
Expand a hostname or domain attribute. Configure known DKIM selectors when available.

validation.command: python -m pytest -q -o log_cli=false tests/test_email_authentication.py tests/test_dns_query.py tests/test_dns.py tests/test_url_dns.py
validation.coverage: Mocked DNS failure and edge cases, strict PyMISP validation, original message-result compatibility, and real dnspython parsing over a local UDP DNS server with a CNAME and split TXT response.
